  "questions": [
    {
      "id": "Q1",
      "category": "K1",
      "question": "Which existing notification channel and observable delivery record represent the requester's resolved-ticket heads-up?",
      "changes": "The close notification's content, recipient, delivery boundary, and acceptance test.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Use the existing outbox, worker, notifier, and resolved-message conventions; observe delivery through the configured notification sink.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must establish the existing resolved-event and relay contracts before notification design and verification."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q2",
      "category": "K2",
      "question": "Which existing lifecycle, notification, report, and client behaviours must remain compatible while close notifications and combined filters are added?",
      "changes": "Regression requirements, implementation boundaries, and compatibility tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Preserve existing lifecycle transitions, error envelope, cursor pagination, report columns, notification delivery and retry behaviour, except for the requested filter correction and close behaviour.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must establish the current contracts and affected consumers before changes are chosen."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q3",
      "category": "K3",
      "question": "What bulk-close and closed-window API contracts already exist, if any, and what request and response shapes, limits, and errors can support 500 tickets?",
      "changes": "Endpoint names, payloads, response semantics, validation, documentation, and HTTP tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "If discovery finds no bulk interface, add a documented bulk-close HTTP operation accepting at least 500 IDs, preserving the existing error envelope; expose the closed window through a documented list filter.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must check routes, clients, body limits, and existing conventions before the API contract is settled."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q4",
      "category": "K4",
      "question": "What counts as a notification the requester 'just got', including pending, sent, failed, dead, and earlier resolution events?",
      "changes": "The suppression interval and event eligibility, including duplicate and missed-notification tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "If no established policy exists, suppress a close notice when a matching resolution notice is pending or was sent within the previous minute; do not treat a dead notice as delivered.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must establish available event timestamps, statuses, and deduplication behaviour before the suppression rule is finalized."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q5",
      "category": "K4",
      "question": "How should immediate delivery and batching interact when a single operation closes multiple tickets, including tickets for different requesters?",
      "changes": "Batch grouping, timing, message shape, and delivery tests.",
      "route": "default",
      "default": "Enqueue immediately and group eligible close notices by requester within one bulk call; deliver on the existing next worker tick without an additional waiting window, and never combine different requesters' ticket details.",
      "blocks": "Nothing: the default proceeds after discovery establishes the notifier and relay contracts."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q6",
      "category": "K4",
      "question": "What exact time window, timestamp, timezone, and boundary inclusivity does the weekly report use for closed tickets?",
      "changes": "The closed-ticket list filter and boundary tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "If discovery finds no established window, use the preceding seven days in UTC, including the lower boundary and excluding times after the query instant, measured from the close transition.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must inspect the report and its inputs first; the checked-in report counts the current data file and does not itself establish a date window."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q7",
      "category": "K3",
      "question": "How should repeated closes and mixed bulk requests reconcile idempotent effects with a 409 for an already-closed ticket?",
      "changes": "Single and bulk response semantics, atomicity, and retry tests.",
      "route": "default",
      "default": "A repeated single close returns 409 with no ticket, audit, or notification change; for bulk requests, validate all entries before mutation and return a conflict without changes if any ticket cannot be closed.",
      "blocks": "Nothing: the default proceeds after discovery checks existing contracts; repeat calls remain idempotent in their effects, not necessarily their responses."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q8",
      "category": "K5",
      "question": "How are actors identified, shared state persisted, notifications exposed, and concurrent changes handled across processes and restarts?",
      "changes": "Audit attribution, privacy assumptions, persistence and concurrency design, and restart tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Use the existing X-Actor header, falling back to system; retain the existing single-owner data-file model and internal-network exposure, without adding authentication or cross-process coordination.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must establish the current actor, storage, visibility, and ownership contracts before deciding how new state survives restarts."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q9",
      "category": "K6",
      "question": "Which runtime, configuration, worker settings, and dependency restrictions govern the service and a 500-ticket request?",
      "changes": "Runtime compatibility, payload sizing, worker behaviour, and test setup.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Use Node.js 22 or later and standard-library modules only; preserve existing configuration defaults and worker-off behaviour.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must verify request-size and configuration limits before the bulk interface and its tests are fixed."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q10",
      "category": "K7",
      "question": "Which existing store, query, audit, notification, and worker seams can implement the outcomes without changing outbox retry logic?",
      "changes": "Module boundaries and isolated tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Keep ticket mutations and audit/outbox enqueueing in the store, query parsing in the query layer, and delivery in the existing worker.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must inspect persistence validation and notification contracts before selecting the seams."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q11",
      "category": "K8",
      "question": "Which tests and running-server checks prove the close, suppression, batching, filters, audit, restart, and 500-ticket outcomes at their actual boundaries?",
      "changes": "The exit evidence and verification commands.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Run the existing npm test suite and add meaningful boundary checks, including a real HTTP server with its worker and observable notification sink.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must establish test helpers and environment capabilities before selecting exact checks; the current intake may not start a server."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q12",
      "category": "K9",
      "question": "What delivery access and execution environment are available after intake for modifying the checkout and verifying a running service?",
      "changes": "Delivery and verification steps.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Deliver the change in the requested repository checkout; do not assume deployment authority or production access.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must establish writable workspace and server-running access before implementation and live verification; this intake is read-only."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q13",
      "category": "K10",
      "question": "What practical responsiveness and privacy bounds can be verified for 500 closures without an agreed numerical latency target?",
      "changes": "Bulk performance checks and notification grouping safeguards.",
      "route": "experiment",
      "default": "Require a successful 500-ticket bulk operation and prompt enqueueing without setting an invented latency service level; keep batches scoped to one requester.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must establish the bulk contract and available test environment before measurement; no experiment is authorized in intake."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q14",
      "category": "K11",
      "question": "Which early checks expose the main risks: incorrect filter conjunction, duplicate or lost notices, incomplete bulk changes, and incompatibility with persisted data or the relay?",
      "changes": "Risk-driven verification and any delivery blocker.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Treat those cases as required checks, including pending versus sent notifications, failures, restart, mixed filters, and a 500-ticket call.",
      "blocks": "Discovery must establish persisted-state and relay contracts before the full risk checks are defined."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q15",
      "category": "K11",
      "question": "If an optional overnight-style loop is used, what finite cap prevents unattended execution from running away?",
      "changes": "The optional loop's stop condition and handoff.",
      "route": "default",
      "default": "Do not use an overnight loop unless useful; if used, stop after 20 iterations or two hours, whichever comes first, and report remaining failures.",
      "blocks": "Nothing: the default proceeds; the required until-loop exit remains green tests and demonstrated running-server behaviour."
    }
  ],
  "summary": "S1 [fact]: The target is the help-desk ticket service in this folder, with the repository checkout as the delivery target. S2 [fact; Q1, Q4]: Closing a ticket should notify its requester in the established style while suppressing a sufficiently recent notice. S3 [fact; Q5]: Notifications should be prompt and bulk closures should avoid spamming through reasonable batching. S4 [fact; Q6]: The list API needs a closed-ticket window based on the weekly-report convention; that convention remains to be established. S5 [fact]: List filters must combine according to the API documentation. S6 [fact]: Verify the existing combination; inspection found the implementation uses any-match while the documentation specifies all-match. S7 [fact; Q11]: A later stage must back-chain before an until loop whose exit requires green tests and demonstrated behaviour against a running server. S8 [fact; Q15]: An overnight-style loop is optional and must have a finite cap. S9 [fact]: Verification must exercise real behaviour and documentation must be accurate and economical. S10 [fact]: Outbox retry logic is outside the change; the planned move away from OldTracker is context, not a migration request. S11 [fact]: Keep the service free of added dependencies. S12 [fact; Q7, Q8]: Repeated close effects must be idempotent, an already-closed ticket must produce 409, and the close audit must identify the actor. S13 [fact; Q3, Q13]: Closing 500 tickets in one bulk call must work and remain responsive without an invented numerical latency target. Discovery leads [hints, not verified external sources]: the help-desk team and support leads, the local API and operations documentation, decision records, report script, notification relay contract, tests, and any accessible team channels or internal documentation; ambiguous terms are 'just got', 'right away', 'batch', and 'weekly window'. Interaction and state [fact; Q8]: agents act through HTTP using X-Actor or the system fallback; requesters receive notifications; the service has shared ticket, audit, and outbox state in one process, optionally persisted across restarts, and exposes an internal outbox endpoint; authentication, per-user visibility, and broader cross-process coordination are not established. [Assumption]: Retain that runtime model and do not add authentication or cross-process coordination unless discovery establishes an existing requirement. Authority and visibility [fact]: This exercise authorizes read-only intake only, with no implementation or server start; a later authorized run targets the named checkout, whose source snapshot remains unchanged until final return in an isolated run. The outcome becomes usable in the returned checkout after implementation and verification; it exists in any deployed service only after a separately authorized release."
